\subsection{The limit tracks periodicity, not length}

Figure~\ref{fig:main}(a) is the paper's sharpest test. Each control carries its
twin's carrier and word count, the $k$ copies of one word becoming non-adjacent
distinct ones; were the failure about length, attention span, exposure bias or a
duration budget the two curves would coincide. They do not. Below $k\!=\!6$ every model is
essentially exact; above it, repeated items are rendered with a median count
error of \ErrRepCk{}\% per checkpoint against \ErrCtl{}\%
$[\ErrCtlLo{},\ErrCtlHi{}]$ for controls ($n=\ErrCtlN{}$), at every $k$ to $32$
and for every model. The contrast is sharpest in exactly-correct renderings:
\ExactCtl{}\% for controls against \ExactRep{}\% for their twins.

\emph{Our \NModels{} checkpoints are only \NFamilies{} architecture families},
so we model the clustering rather than count checkpoints. By family the gap is
\FamExact{} $[\FamExactLo{},\FamExactHi{}]$ points, all three positive; by
checkpoint \CkExact{} $[\CkExactLo{},\CkExactHi{}]$, positive in all
\CkExactNPos{} --- including the one whose median-error gap is zero, which still
renders repeated items exactly \CkRevExact{} points less often than its controls
(Table~\ref{tab:models}). A mixed-effects linear probability model with
architecture as a random effect and checkpoint nested inside it puts the gap at
\MixArm{} points, and \MixAllClear{} six interval constructions exclude zero,
the widest being $[\MixLo{},\MixHi{}]$. Partial pooling answers what three
families cannot: the posterior predictive gap for an architecture
\emph{outside} the panel is \BayesNewFam{}
$[\BayesNewFamLo{},\BayesNewFamHi{}]$, $P{=}\BayesNewFamP{}$ --- enough to
place the effect, not to exclude a fourth architecture lacking it, and under the
widest prior on the group-level scales it touches zero
($\BayesWidePriorLo{}$, $P{=}\BayesWidePriorP{}$). We then acquired a fourth architecture.
CosyVoice~2, whose alignment supervision makes it the design most likely to be
immune, renders repeated text exactly \CosyRep{}\% against \CosyCtl{}\% for its
controls ($n=\CosyN{}$): a gap of \CosyGap{} points, inside the predicted
interval and near its \BayesNewFam{} mean, from a fit committed before the
checkpoint's first waveform existed (commit \texttt{6f34945}, so the ordering is
checkable rather than asserted; S16). That interval is wide, and the agreement
closer than it entitles us to expect. Across \SpecN{} specifications
spanning every forking choice we made --- exclusions, $k$ threshold, cycled
against never-cycled controls, seed subset, aggregation and outcome definition
--- the gap runs \SpecLo{}--\SpecHi{} points and none reverses its
sign. These are not independent tests and we correct across none of them: the
curve is a robustness envelope over one comparison, not a family of hypotheses,
and our claims rest on effect sizes, not $p$-values (S11).

\emph{Periodicity, or verbatim identity?} The two vary together above, so we ran
a ladder holding carrier, word count and requested count fixed and varying only
the period $p$. The deficit is \emph{graded}: exact rates rise \PerPOne{},
\PerPTwo{}, \PerPFour{}, \PerPEight{}\% at $p=1,2,4,8$, monotone in all
\PerNCk{} checkpoints ($n=\PerNKept{}$). The decisive cell is $p\!=\!2$, where no token
is ever adjacent to itself and half the deficit remains: \PerDTwo{} against
\PerDOne{} points, a surviving fraction of \PerRatioScan{} on the
strictest of \PerNRules{} rules and \PerRatioRecLo{}--\PerRatioRecHi{} on the
recount rules, which is where we rest the claim: the strict margin over one half
is thin, and the $p\!=\!1$ arm's shorter audio and higher cap-hit rate both push
that particular ratio up (S28). So it is periodicity, not verbatim identity, nor a
failure to tell neighbours apart: a comma, full stop or ``and'' between
repetitions recovers \DisR{}\%.

Never-cycled control fillers throughout put the gap at \ApHeadCk{} by checkpoint
and \ApHeadFam{} by family against \ApHeadCkCyc{} and \ApHeadFamCyc{} cycled,
positive throughout, and we quote the smaller --- though most of that
\ApHeadDrop{} points is vocabulary rather than periodicity, the substitution
costing \ApHeadTolDrop{} within one unit and nothing at all on median error.

\subsection{Not the decoding rule, the judge, or our exclusions}

The families ship repetition penalties differing by an order of magnitude, and a
penalty suppresses repeated tokens directly. Swept on \PenNArch{} architectures
the deficit stays put (XTTS-v2 \PenRepLo{}--\PenRepHi{}\% exact over a
\PenFold{}-fold range, Qwen3-TTS-0.6B \PenQRepLo{}--\PenQRepHi{}\% over
\PenQFold{}-fold, S15), and the \PenNoneN{} Llasa checkpoints pass \emph{no}
penalty and show it at full size. Nor is it
sampling: greedy decoding gives \GreedyGap{} points against \GreedySampGap{}
sampled (S22). Nor our exclusions: with every rule off the gap is
\ExSensAll{} points against \ExSensPanel{}, and the one rule falling unevenly --- our token
budget, dropping \ExclCapRep{}\% of repeated generations against
\ExclCapCtl{}\% of controls --- works against the contrast, truncated counts
being censored downward (S18).

Nor is it the recogniser, the objection this design most has to answer: CTC
blank-collapse merges adjacent identical words, depressing repeated but not
control counts --- an artifact with the effect's own periodicity signature. Re-scoring the \emph{same} audio with
\IndNJudges{} recognisers --- a second CTC model with different
pretraining, a robust-finetuned one, and Whisper, whose autoregressive decoder
has no blank-collapse mechanism at all --- leaves the gap at
\IndGapLo{}--\IndGapHi{} points, positive in all \IndNCkPos{} of \IndNCk{}
checkpoints and every family under every judge. Decisive is which arm moves:
across them the repeated arm's exact rate spans \IndRepSpread{} points
(\IndRepLo{}--\IndRepHi{}\%) against the control arm's \IndCtlSpread{}.
Changing the scorer moves the arm the models get \emph{right} --- word error
rate --- and leaves the arm they get wrong fixed, where a judge-side collapse
predicts the reverse. Disagreements do concentrate on repeated items, but with
the \emph{opposite} sign to the confound --- $+\IndAsym{}$ where the artifact
requires $\IndAsymThresh{}$ --- so our judge under-states the deficit rather
than manufacturing it (S14). VITS~\cite{kim2021vits} shows \emph{no} dissociation
through the same recogniser on the same strings (\VitsRep{}\% against
\VitsCtl{}\%, $n=90$, a gap of \VitsGap{} against the panel's
$+\ARPoolGap{}$), and not for want of competence (S13); blank-collapse would
have depressed its repeated items too.

F5-TTS~\cite{chen2024f5tts}, flow-matching rather than recurrent, \emph{does}
show it: \FivettsRep{}\% against \FivettsCtl{}\%, $+\FivettsGap{}$, growing
with $k$ as the panel's does. Absence of an autoregressive decoder confers no
immunity, and we withdraw the architectural claim an earlier draft made. What
plausibly separates the two is where the count must live: VITS gives each input token its own duration, while F5-TTS estimates
one total duration and so must represent how much speech to make. Supplying F5-TTS the duration a correct rendering
takes splits the deficit: below $k\!=\!\DurSplit{}$ it lifts exact renderings
\DurLoFree{}\% to \DurLoFixed{}\%, at or above it the gain is \DurHiGain{}
($n=\DurHiN{}$, any gain above \EqDurBound{} points excluded) --- handed the
right length the model still cannot place thirty-two repetitions in it (S13). S20 lists three further rivals.

The $k\!\ge\!6$ threshold was chosen after seeing where the arms diverge, which
is why the abstract gives the unconditioned figure too and the specification
curve varies it. Two exploratory analyses, dated in S16, are reported in
text alone (S8, S10, S17). Within $k\le32$ the deficit is proportional, not
saturating (RSS \ShapePropSSE{} against \ShapeSatSSE{}), so no horizon lies in
this ladder; extending to $k\!\le\!128$ lowers the fitted saturation
scale \HzRatio{}-fold, but form-dependently (\HzFormLo{}--\HzFormHi{}) and not
unanimously (\HzRevNames{} inverts it). Neither that nor the rate of
effective-rank gain distinguishes a horizon from any saturating process.
